read_scope.notes: Read the complete 22-page supplied PDF through layout-preserving extraction and visually inspected every rendered page, including Figures 1–6, Tables 1–8, references and Appendices A–G. Consulted the snapshot paper.tex and specificity_results.tex to resolve notation and locate passages. The abstract has 155 whitespace-delimited words in its source. Did not inspect other reviews, earlier assessments, the current working-tree manuscript, or goal/progress records.

score_reasons.expression: The English is fluent and generally precise, with useful distinctions such as the theoretical no-contrast predictor versus the observed generic arm (Section 4.2), and point estimates versus resolved comparisons (Section 5.1). The opening Monet–Sisley example is economical and effective. Repeated qualifications about artistic fidelity, scene adherence and descriptive status, along with phrases such as single stacked reference configuration and global cross-repeat-corrected named/free squared change, make otherwise clear prose more laborious than necessary. Q is described as magnitude where squared magnitude would be more precise.
score_reasons.structure: The question, experimental arms, feature representation, estimands and primary results follow a coherent progression. Detailed feature definitions and historical cohorts appropriately sit in appendices, and retrospective analyses are explicitly identified. The main narrative nevertheless carries several different diagnostic tracks at once: Section 5.3 moves from ranking reversals to historical class differences and half-split controls, while Section 5.4 ends with primary-error sensitivities under a distributional-proximity heading. The large common component, prominent in the title and abstract, arrives relatively late, and Table 3 is separated from its initial discussion by substantial unrelated material.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The abstract communicates the design, reference collection and bounded conclusion without requiring the repository. Table 1 usefully translates feature families, and the D = 0 and D = 1 benchmarks prevent a major interpretive mistake. However, the central method begins with heavily indexed vectors and multiple decompositions before providing a simple example, which itself remains symbolic. Alignment, aligned amplitude, squared contrast magnitude and calibrated error require repeated cross-reference. A newcomer can recover the argument, but the main tables and Figure 2 do not yet make that recovery easy.
score_reasons.engagement: The motivating question is consequential and the original/generated image panel rewards inspection. Uneven Monet–Sisley response and the reversal between uncalibrated and calibrated model ordering give the paper a discernible, interesting narrative. Momentum is reduced by the long numerical diagnostic passages and recurring prohibitions on interpretation. Figure 2 largely identifies its encodings without guiding inspection, and the Discussion predominantly restates results and boundaries rather than giving a compact affirmative account of what this audit teaches an evaluator.

strengths: The opening example makes a subtle evaluation problem concrete: greater proximity to Monet can accompany the same improvement toward Sisley, so proximity alone cannot establish the intended artist distinction.

Sections 3.1–3.3 clearly distinguish digital reproductions, equal painter weighting, a separate development scaler and the fixed common-scene design. Table 1 gives accessible interpretations without pretending the coordinates measure physical paint.
Section 4.2 supplies interpretable no-contrast and exact-agreement benchmarks, explains negative finite estimates, and distinguishes labeled agreement from mere separation.

The manuscript consistently marks post-result analyses and source corrections, reports the source correction that weakens the Sunburst comparison, and retains the contrary prospective result in Appendix F.
Figure 1 is legible and visually informative; Figure 3 efficiently displays all six artist pairs rather than selecting only the conspicuous Monet–Sisley result.
The final conclusions remain bounded to the measured collection and recorded configurations, and the availability statement is candid about the remaining exact-pixel access limitation.

findings.issue: The reader reaches mu, r, H, z, d, beta, D, e and theta, with stacked configurations and two decompositions, before receiving an intuitive worked account of what is compared. The late example 0, r and 2r presupposes the same abstraction it is intended to explain.
findings.reader_effect: A graduate reader unfamiliar with this representation can understand individual definitions while missing the distinction between a common shift, correct-direction response strength and total labeled disagreement. That distinction is needed to interpret every main result.
findings.suggested_change: Begin Section 4 with a short plain-language route through the calculation: record 31 properties per image; subtract the four-painter average; compare the remaining four labeled differences with the corresponding historical differences. Recast the existing 0/r/2r example in words as no artist differences, matching differences and doubled differences, with errors 1/0/1. Explain that multiplying discrepancies from independent repeats removes the average contribution of nonrecurring sampling noise. Keep Equations 1–3 and their benchmarks in the main text, but move the residual derivation in Equation 4 and the redundant regression equation to Appendix B to fund the explanation within 22 pages.

findings.issue: Section 5.3 combines scene/calibration ranking changes with reference-class departures and detailed genuine-painting controls. Section 5.4 combines common changes, energy/spread results and sensitivities of the primary contrast error. These are separate questions under headings that do not cover the full contents.
findings.reader_effect: The reader repeatedly switches targets and denominators and can lose track of which result explains the primary finding, which changes the target and which assesses source robustness. The shared-change result promised by the title and abstract is also delayed until Section 5.4.
findings.suggested_change: Keep the primary alignment/error result first, then give the common-change result a concise, clearly located paragraph before the retrospective pair and calibration diagnostics. Restrict the scene/calibration subsection to the two ordering changes. Group class/measurement/source sensitivities together, and reduce the half-split-control passage to its main lesson with the numerical ranges retained in Appendix C. Make these moves and cuts instead of adding a new overview section.

findings.issue: The principal comparison table reports differences against GPT Image 2, so neither of the two resolved FLUX comparisons appears in it. The calibration table uses mostly symbolic headers and omits the uncalibrated D values, requiring readers to move between tables to verify the central ordering reversal.
findings.reader_effect: The displays do not directly answer the comparison questions emphasized in the prose. A reader must reconstruct the primary superiority statements and then remember earlier error values while interpreting the calibration result.
findings.suggested_change: Use the existing Table 6 contrasts to show the relevant FLUX comparisons in the main display, clearly retaining the original fixed family and avoiding any new testing. Redesign Table 3 around plain-language columns for uncalibrated scene error, error of the across-scene mean, scene variation and calibrated error. Move Q and the alignment ratio to the appendix or a compact note. Place the revised table with its first discussion and state explicitly that calibrated values are retrospective estimates from held-out scenes.

findings.issue: The abstract places weak Monet–Sisley alignment and the calibration ordering change alongside the primary result without identifying either as a retrospective diagnostic, although Sections 4.5 and 5 do identify their status.
findings.reader_effect: A reader of the standalone abstract can reasonably assume all three findings came from the same declared analysis plan and give the ordering change more evidential status than the main text warrants.
findings.suggested_change: Use a compact phrase such as Post-result diagnostics found weak Monet–Sisley alignment in five models and changed the lowest-error model after scalar calibration. Rebalance the surrounding sentences to preserve the 155-word maximum; do not append an extra sentence to the current 155-word abstract.

findings.location: Section 4.5, p. 7, and Section 5.3, p. 9; paper.tex lines 373–386 and specificity_results.tex lines 73–82
findings.issue: Q is introduced through an inner-product formula but is called generated contrast magnitude in the results. It is a corrected squared magnitude relative to the reference, whereas the scalar calibration changes the contrasts themselves.
findings.reader_effect: The reader can mistake Q = 2.223 for a 2.223-fold amplitude response and may not see why shrinking GPT Image 2 contrasts improves error despite its near-unit aligned slope.
findings.suggested_change: Call Q corrected squared contrast magnitude at both introduction and interpretation. Translate the fitted scalar into one concrete sentence using the already reported folds: GPT Image 2 differences are uniformly reduced to about 45% of their measured size before evaluation on the omitted scene. Retain the qualification that this rescales measured vectors and is not an implemented image operation.

findings.location: Figure 2 and its introductory paragraph/caption, p. 8; specificity_results.tex lines 23–33
findings.issue: The figure is readable, but its text mostly names the encodings and states what separation cannot establish. It does not tell a newcomer how to read agreement or identify the salient reference configuration in the display.
findings.reader_effect: The reader sees clusters but must infer that each generated mean should approach the cross of the same color and that matching a single visible separation is insufficient. This weakens the figure as an explanation of the core metric.
findings.suggested_change: Replace part of the repeated caveat with a reading instruction: compare each colored circle with the cross of the same color, then compare the full four-color arrangement. Point out the visible separation of the Cézanne reference from the other references along the first axis and direct attention to the Monet–Sisley distinction developed in Figure 3. Retain the two-dimensional projection limitation and avoid translating the plot into a perceptual claim.

findings.location: Introduction, Sections 4–6 and Conclusion, pp. 1 and 5–12
findings.issue: The manuscript repeatedly restates that measured differences are not validated artistic fidelity, that descriptive checks are not new tests and that fixed scenes do not establish content-conditional fidelity. These cautions are individually justified, but their recurrence often ends paragraphs that could instead advance interpretation.
findings.reader_effect: The prose becomes defensive and slows the reader after the relevant limit is already understood. The Discussion and Conclusion give relatively little additional synthesis beyond the preceding results.
findings.suggested_change: Keep each essential qualification at the point where the corresponding misunderstanding arises, plus one consolidated scope paragraph. Cut near-duplicate caveats in neighboring result captions and the Discussion. Use the recovered space for a short affirmative synthesis: an evaluation of artist names should report common change, direction/strength of labeled contrasts and target mismatch separately because they answer different questions in this experiment. Preserve all qualifications that change the interpretation of a specific estimate.

findings.location: Data and code availability, p. 12; paper.tex lines 455–456; Appendix D, p. 18
findings.issue: The availability statement says Appendix D displays 36 generated and four reference examples. Appendix D displays the 12 control images; the other 24 generated and four reference images are in main-text Figure 1.
findings.reader_effect: The cross-reference sends a reader looking for the complete example panel to the wrong location.
findings.suggested_change: Replace Appendix D displays with Figures 1 and 4 display. State separately that Appendix D explains their selection and that the manifest records identities and hashes.

claim_fidelity_issues: The abstract does not mark its artist-pair and calibration findings as post-result diagnostics, although the main text does; their status should be carried into the standalone summary.
Section 5.3 calls Q contrast magnitude rather than corrected squared contrast magnitude, leaving room for an incorrect amplitude interpretation.

No unqualified claim of perceptual artistic fidelity, internal mechanism identification or a uniquely best generator was found. The source-correction and contrary-transfer qualifications are preserved.
summary: A competent, carefully bounded empirical narrative with fluent English, a strong opening motivation and informative figures. It is not yet effortless for the intended new reader: the metric introduction is too abstract, diagnostic tracks interrupt the results hierarchy, and the central ordering comparison must be assembled across displays. An intuition-first method explanation, tighter placement of diagnostics and a consolidated comparison table would materially improve comprehension and pace without new experiments or exceeding the page limit.
